stem: An example of physical change –
expl: Physical changes usually affect the form of a chemical substance, but not its chemical composition. This fact contrasts with the concept of chemical change in which the chemical composition of the substance changes or one or more substances combines or break up to form new substances. In general, a physical change is using physical means. For example, sugar dissolved in water can be recovered by allowing the water to evaporate.

stem: Change of water into the vapour is called –
expl: Change of water into the vapour is a physical change.

stem: Which of the following is an example of chemical change–

options.label: a
options.text: Dispersion of white light into the light of 7 colours when passed through a prism

options.label: c
options.text: Wet soil lump, when dried, gets fragile

expl: A change which alters the specific properties of a material by bringing about a change in its molecular composition, followed by a change in state, is called a chemical change. The chemical change is a change in which something new is formed. Cooking of vegetables is a chemical change as it brings irreversible changes in the composition of vegetables.

stem:
Which of the following is/are the example/examples of chemical change?
1. Crystallization of sodium chloride
2. Melting of ice
3. Souring of milk
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
expl: A chemical change is a change in which something new is formed (usually irreversible). The starting materials change into an entirely different substance or substances. This new substance has a different chemical composition than the starting materials. Examples of chemical change would be the reaction of iron with air (rusting) or the reaction of a metal and acid. The crystallization of sodium chloride and melting of ice, both are the examples of a physical change while souring of milk is an example of chemical change.

stem: Detect the odd one :

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Ripening of fruits, setting of cement and burning of coal-all of these are chemical changes and all are also exothermic. So there is no difference. Hence, option (e) is the correct answer.

stem:
Assertion (A) : A chemical reaction becomes faster at a higher temperature.
Reason (R) : At higher temperature, molecular motion becomes more rapid.

options.label: a
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: b
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not a correct explanation of (A).

expl: A chemical reaction generally becomes faster at a higher temperature because at higher temperature, molecular motion becomes more rapid and the molecules have higher kinetic energy. The process of a chemical reaction depends on the concentration, temperature and physical state of molecules and their nature. Normally, higher the temperature of molecules, faster would be the reaction. Hence, both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

stem: What form of energy is produced in the decomposition of water?
expl: Hydrolysis is the chemical reaction in which ions of a salt dissolved in water, mutually combines with a water molecule to form an acidic or basic solution and the energy produced in this process is in the form of heat.

stem: Pasteurization is a process by which –

options.label: a
options.text: Milk is preserved at a very low temperature for 24 hours

options.label: c
options.text: First milk is heated up to a longer time and then cooled suddenly within specified time

expl: In order to pasteurize milk, first, the milk is heated up to a longer time and then cooled suddenly within specified time. Pasteurization is a process invented by French scientist Louis Pasteur during the nineteenth century. In 1864, Louis Pasteur discovered that heating beer and wine was enough to kill most of the bacteria that caused spoilage and hence, prevented these beverages from turning sour. This was achieved by eliminating pathogenic microbes and lowering microbial numbers to prolong the quality of the beverage.

stem: Pasteurization is related to :
expl: The Pasteurization is a process that kills microbes (mainly bacteria) in food and drinks such as milk and facilitates its preservation and safety. In this process, the milk is heated at about 630 C for 30 minutes or, alternatively, at about 720 C for 15 seconds to ensure that any harmful bacteria is not alive. The process was invented by the French scientist Louis Pasteur. So it is called Pasteurization.

stem: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
expl: Pasteurization is the partial sterilization of a product, such as milk, wine or fruit juices to make it safe for consumption and improve its keeping quality. Pasteurization was developed by Louis Pasteur in 1864. It is not used for tea. Other pairs are correctly matched.

stem: Phosphatase test is used for the analysis of :
expl: Phosphatase test is commonly used for the analysis of milk and dairy products. The alkaline phosphatase (ALP) is an enzyme normally present in raw milk and it is inactivated in conditions of heat treatment. The temperature of inactivation of ALP is slightly higher than that required for the destruction of pathogenic bacteria. So the ALP test in pasteurized milk is used to verify if the heating process of pasteurization is done correctly. Phosphatase test is also used for checking the pollution of water. Acid phosphatase test proves superior to standard phenotypic identification procedure for Clostridium perfringens (It is used as an indicator for persistent faecal pollution as well as to monitor the efficacy of water treatment processes) strains isolated from water. ALP test may also be used for checking the quality of milk tea. It may be the reason that MPPSC has given answer (d) for this question in its final answer key. An ALP blood test is also used for screening, diagnosis, and monitoring of liver or bone diseases and other health conditions. Alkaline phosphatase (ALP) enzyme is present in many parts of the body, but it is primarily found in the liver, bones, intestine, and kidneys. ALP testing measures the amount of this enzyme in the blood. Abnormal levels of ALP can be caused by liver or bone conditions and other types of health problems.

stem: Because of impurities the boiling point of a liquid –
expl: The boiling point of a liquid is the temperature at which its vapour pressure is equal to the pressure of the gas above it. When some impurities are mixed with any liquid, its boiling point increases.

stem: The amount of solute present per unit volume or per unit mass of the solution/solvent is known as ____ in Chemistry.
expl: The amount of solute present per unit volume or per unit mass of the solution/solvent is called 'Concentration of Solution'. The concentration of a solution is the measure of how much solute is present in a fixed amount (mass or volume) of the solution or the amount of solute dissolved in a given mass or volume of solvent.

stem: For two liquids A and B to form an ideal solution :

options.label: a
options.text: Entropy of mixing must be zero

options.label: b
options.text: Free energy of mixing should be zero

options.label: c
options.text: Enthalpy of mixing should be zero

expl: An ideal solution is a homogeneous mixture where the interactions between solute and solvent molecules are identical to those between the pure components. This means that the intermolecular forces between solute and solvent molecules are roughtly the same as the intermolecular forces between solute-solute and solvent-solvent molecules. For an ideal solution, the enthalpy of mixing (ΔH ) is zero. The enthalpy of mixing (ΔH ) is the change in enthalpy that occurs when a substance is mixed with another substance or when a solution is formed. In an ideal solution, since the interactions between molecules are similar, there is no net change in energy when the components are mixed. Therefore, the enthalpy of mixing is zero. This means that when the components of an ideal solution are mixed, there is no heat absorbed or released. In essence, the molecules mix without any energy change. The ideal solution follows Raoult's Law, which states that the partial vapour pressure of each component in the solution is directly proportional to its mole fraction.

stem: The conductivity of a strong electrolyte :
expl: The conductivity of a strong electrolyte generally decreases slightly on dilution. Conductivity of an electrolyte solution is directly related to the concentration and mobility of ions in the solution. Strong electrolytes, like strong acids, strong bases, and soluble ionic salts, completely dissociate into ions when dissolved. When a strong electrolyte solution is diluted, the volume of the solution increases while the number of ions remains relatively constant. This leads to a decrease in the concentration of ions per unit volume. While dilution increases the distance between ions and slightly improves their mobility, the decrease in ion concentration outweighs this effect in strong electrolytes, resulting in a net decrease in conductivity. Examples of strong electrolytes are NaCl, KCl, etc.

stem:
Given below are two statements, one is labelled as
Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : A solution of table salt in a glass of water is homogeneous.
Reason (R) : A solution having different compositions throughout is homogeneous.
Select the correct answer from the code given below :

stem: Water passes from the soil into the roots by a physical process called :

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The plants absorb water from the soil with the help of root hairs through osmosis. The diffusion of water molecules through a semi-permeable membrane is called osmosis. The water moves into root hair cells by osmosis, as there is a high concentration of minerals/sugars in the cells, and a little water. This decreases the water potential inside the cell, so water molecules move down gradient into the cells. The water can then be moved by xylem in the transpiration stream through the plant and out of its leaves.

stem: After cutting cucumber if salt is added, then water comes out due to :
expl: Osmosis is the process when water (or solvent) molecules move from a region (solution) of low concentration to a region (solution) of higher concentration through a semipermeable membrane. When salt is applied to cucumber or cut onion pieces, it makes their surrounding more concentrated than the concentration of their cell sap. Then it causes the water molecules in the cells of the cucumber and the cut onion pieces to move to the surrounding through their cell membrane (which is semipermeable).

stem:
Consider the following statements :
1. During the process of osmosis, the solvent travels from the concentrated solution to the dilute solution.
2. In the reverse osmosis, external pressure is applied to the dilute solution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
expl: In the process of osmosis, the solvent moves through a semi-permeable membrane into a region of higher solute concentration from lower concentration that tends to equalize the solute concentration on both sides. While in reverse osmosis, we apply external pressure upon concentrated solution to reverse the movement of solvent, i.e. from more concentrated to weaker dilute solution. This technique is used to purify the solution by making it free from impurities. Hence, both given statements are incorrect.

stem:
Consider the following statements with reference to osmosis :
(1) If the semipermeable membrane is placed between the solvent and solution, the solvent molecules will flow through the membrane from pure solvent to the solution.
(2) The process of flow of solvent is called as reverse osmosis.
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
expl: If the semipermeable membrane is placed between the solvent and solution, the solvent molecules will flow through the membrane from pure solvent (lower concentration) to the solution (higher concentration). This process of flow of solvent is called osmosis, not reverse osmosis. Hence, only statement (1) is correct.

stem: Which one of the following processes is NOT useful for purification of solid impurities?
expl: Distillation is the action of purifying a liquid by a process of heating and cooling. Distillation is generally used for purification of liquid impurities while sublimation and crystallization are used for purification of solid impurities.

stem: The technique of chromatography is used to –

options.label: d
options.text: Separate the substances from a mixture

expl: Chromatography is a separation technique used to separate the different components in a liquid mixture. The separation is based on differential partitioning between the mobile and stationary phases. Chromatography may be preparative or analytical. The purpose of preparative chromatography is to separate the components of a mixture for more advanced use and thus it is a form of purification.

stem: Process of solid camphor into camphor vapour is called:
expl: Solid camphor directly changes into camphor vapour and this process is called sublimation. The sublimation is the process in which some substances upon heating directly changes into vapour form and when cooled again directly turns into solid form.

stem: A sample of any of the following substances disappears after sometime when exposed to air like camphor, naphthalene or dry ice. This phenomenon is called :
expl: Sublimation is the transition of a substance directly from the solid to the gas phase, without passing through the intermediate liquid phase. Substances like camphor, naphthalene or dry ice (solid carbon dioxide) display this phenomenon.

stem: The conversion of a solid directly into gas is called as :

options.label: e

expl: Sublimation is the transition of a substance directly from the solid to the gas phase, without passing through the intermediate liquid phase. Substances like camphor, naphthalene or dry ice (solid carbon dioxide) display this phenomenon.

stem: A mixture of sand and naphthalene can be separated by :

options.label: d
options.text: fractional distillation (d) None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: Naphthalene displays the phenomenon of sublimation, which is the transition of a substance directly from the solid to gas phase upon heating. Hence, a mixture of sand and naphthalene can be separated by sublimation.

stem: Which of the following slows down the reaction rate?
expl: Catalytic promoter or accelerators are those substances used to increase the activity of catalysts positively. Reactions that are facilitated by catalysts can be divided into two major classes : homogeneous catalysis and heterogeneous catalysis. A homogeneous catalyst is present in the same phase as the reactants. A heterogeneous catalyst is present in a different phase from the reactants. All of these facilitate reactions. Hence, option (d) is correct.

stem:
Which of the following are exothermic processes ?
(i) Evaporation of water.
(ii) Dilution of an acid (HSO). 2 4
(iii) Reaction of water with quick lime.
(iv) Sublimation of camphor (crystals).
expl: Exothermic reactions or processes release heat. When quicklime (CaO) reacts with water, it forms calcium hydroxide [Ca(OH)] and release a large amount of heat. This reaction is highly exothermic. When a concentrated acid is diluted with water, heat is released. This is also an exothermic process, particularly for strong acids like Sulfuric acid (HSO). Evaporation of water and sublimation of camphor 2 4 are both endothermic reactions, meaning they absorb heat from their surroundings to proceed.

stem: Which of the following pairs will give displacement reactions ?
expl: A chemical reaction in which a more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal is called displacement reaction. Copper is more reactive than silver, meaning it has a stronger tendency to lose electrons. When copper metal is placed in a silver nitrate solution, a displacement reaction occurs where copper replaces silver, forming copper nitrate and solid silver.

stem: Example of corrosion is –
expl: Gradual decay of metals by air or chemical substances is called corrosion. Rusting on iron i.e. brown coating on iron, green coating on copper and black coating on silver, all these are examples of corrosion.
